clue.text: A second Caxton, perhaps, and no slowcoach

parts.note: William Caxton was England's first printer, so he is an example of one

explanation.surface: Another early printer appears, and this one works fast.
explanation.walkthrough: William Caxton brought the printing press to England in the 1470s.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprinter is a fast runner, the opposite of a slowcoach.

clue.text: Client wants us to meet the Queen

parts.note: taken as written
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A customer demands an audience with the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is a customer or consumer of a service, much as a client is.

clue.text: Upheaval involving architect with the church

parts.note: Sir Christopher Wren, architect of St Paul's Cathedral

explanation.surface: An architect's involvement in a church project causes disruption.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrench is a sudden violent twist or a painful emotional upheaval, such as leaving home.

clue.text: Rattle change in another way — that should keep us warm

indicators.note: arranging the letters in another way signals that the preceding words are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone suggests shuffling coins differently, as if that could warm the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' does double service in the surface reading, but in the wordplay it is part of the fodder RATTLE CHANGE IN, with 'another way' as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A home heating system piped from one boiler exists precisely to keep the occupants warm.

clue.text: Immature aloofness almost leads to beauty

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a chill in someone's manner is coolness or aloofness
a dish is slang for an attractive person, a beauty

explanation.surface: Playing hard to get only half works when wooing an attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: Childish behaviour is immature, like that of a child.

clue.text: Perhaps Jack will get fit and famous

parts.note: in bridge the jack is one of the honour cards, along with ace, king, queen and ten
fit to do something means able to do it

explanation.surface: A sailor will become healthy and celebrated.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack suggests a sailor or a man's name; here it is the playing card, one of the honours in bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Honourable once meant illustrious, worthy of high renown, which is close to famous.

clue.text: Splits always seen in steamship

indicators.note: seen in means the letters for always appear inside those for steamship

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: Divisions are a permanent feature aboard a steamer.
explanation.definitionFit: To sever is to cut apart, so severs is a verb form meaning splits.

clue.text: Look for a poisoner up a never-ending road

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the road word has no ending, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a street is a road in a town

explanation.surface: Searching for a killer along an endless street.
explanation.walkthrough: The UPAS TREE of Java is famed for its poisonous sap; the surface hints at a murderer instead. 'Look for' and 'a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The upas tree yields a toxic latex once used for poison arrows, so it is a poisoner.

clue.text: Rugby player agreed to be housed by a gardener

indicators.note: housed by means the letters for agreed go inside those for the gardener

parts.note: a hoer is someone using a hoe, a gardener
OK means agreed

explanation.surface: A rugby player consents to lodging with someone who tends the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The hooker is the rugby forward in the middle of the front row who hooks the ball in the scrum.

clue.text: Landing stage shown on kind of chart to the right

parts.note: a pie chart is a circular graph divided into slices

explanation.surface: A jetty is marked on a diagram, on the right-hand side.
explanation.definitionFit: A pier is a platform built out into water where boats land.

clue.text: Some love to marry, if prohibited

parts.note: some means not all of them
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
to wed is to marry

explanation.surface: Some people who are in love are barred from marrying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' reads as a quantity of love; it is the phrase NOT ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something banned or forbidden is not permitted, the sense of prohibited.

clue.text: Stiffness of circular crown in hats

indicators.note: going round in a circle suggests the whole combination is turned back to front
in means the crown letters go inside the hats word

parts.note: taken as written
CR is an abbreviation for crown, as on coins

explanation.surface: A round crown worn inside hats gives them their rigidity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circular' looks like it describes the crown's shape; it signals reading the whole assembly backwards, giving HCRATS turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch stiffens fabric, and figuratively means stiffness of manner.

clue.text: Warder gets wino drunk in Hitchcock film

indicators.note: being drunk suggests the letters are reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: A prison guard gets a vagrant intoxicated, like a scene from a thriller.
explanation.definitionFit: Rear Window is Alfred Hitchcock's 1954 thriller starring James Stewart.

clue.text: Beekeeper looks very much like a pianist

definitions.text: Beekeeper looks very much like a pianist

parts.words: Beekeeper looks very much like a pianist
parts.note: a keeper of hives whose title, written down, differs from a keyboard player's by a single letter

explanation.surface: A beekeeper bears a striking resemblance to a piano player.
explanation.walkthrough: The resemblance is in spelling, not appearance: change one letter of A PIANIST to get the beekeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: An apiary is a place where bees are kept, and its keeper has this title.

clue.text: Wide-hipped American woman in the bar

parts.note: broad is American slang for a woman
taken as written
a beam is a long bar of wood or metal

explanation.surface: An American woman sitting in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub; it is a structural beam.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad in the beam is an idiom for having wide hips, from a ship's width.

clue.text: In the main, I quit youthful wickedness

indicators.note: the opening word tells us the answer lies inside the following words

explanation.surface: Someone renounces the sins of youth while out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'main' through 'I quit' into the start of 'youthful'.
explanation.definitionFit: Iniquity is gross injustice or immoral conduct, a synonym of wickedness.

clue.text: See 15
Cut down when one crossed over

parts.note: A means one, as in 'a dog'
to bridge a gap is to cross over it

explanation.surface: Someone was felled while crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: An abridged text has been shortened or cut down.

clue.text: See 4
On holiday we must pack clobber that's pale

parts.note: being off work means being on holiday

indicators.note: pack means the word we is stuffed with the letters for clobber

parts.note: taken as written
to clobber is to hit

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers must pack their gear, which looks rather washed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clobber' is British slang for clothes or gear, but here it is the verb to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-white is a very pale, slightly greyish or yellowish white.

clue.text: FBI agent holding rule to be unsound

indicators.note: holding means the letters for the agent surround those for rule

parts.note: a fed is American slang for a federal agent, as in the FBI
a law is a rule

explanation.surface: A federal agent detaining a suspect proves untrustworthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flawed has defects, so it is unsound.

clue.text: Misbehave when dipping into reserved wine

indicators.note: dipping into means the misbehave letters go inside the reserved word

parts.note: a reserved person is shy
to err is to go astray or misbehave

explanation.surface: Someone behaves badly when sampling wine that has been set aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherry is a fortified wine from Jerez in Spain.

clue.text: Cooks at mess function

indicators.note: the letters are made to function in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Chefs prepare food at a military dining event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' is not the anagram signal; it is fodder, with 'function' as the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To steam food is a way of cooking it, so steams means cooks.

clue.text: A recount is unusual for golfers

indicators.note: unusual suggests the letters are in an out-of-the-ordinary order

explanation.surface: A golf score being counted again is out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: CARNOUSTIE is a Scottish town on the coast of Angus with a famous championship links course.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnoustie is a links course that has hosted the Open, so it is a place for golfers.

clue.text: Old-fashioned person's party fare

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
to fare is to do, as in 'how did you do?'

explanation.surface: An outdated individual brings food to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' reads as food, but it is the verb, to get on.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodo, after the extinct bird, is someone hopelessly behind the times.

clue.text: Girlfriend, starting diet, had food later

indicators.note: later puts the eating after the opening letter
starting means the first letter of diet is taken

parts.note: to eat food in the past is ate

explanation.surface: A girlfriend begins a diet but then eats anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: A date is the person someone is romantically going out with.

clue.text: Account for endless red wine

indicators.note: endless means the word red loses its last letter

parts.note: port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: Explaining a supply of red wine that never runs out.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is a written or spoken account of something.

clue.text: Never mind the gossip about the doctor going back

indicators.note: about means the gossip word surrounds the doctor letters

parts.note: to natter is to chat or gossip

indicators.note: going back means the doctor letters are reversed

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: Forget the chatter about the physician's return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns the doctor's letters to OM before 'about' wraps the gossip word around them.
explanation.definitionFit: No matter is a dismissive phrase meaning it is unimportant, never mind.
